description: Single-case golden benchmark grounded in the supplied customer_trends trace.

important_distinctions: Planned social queries are not collected social evidence.
Snippet-only news is not full-text evidence or customer reviews.
Zero engagement metrics do not prove zero real-world engagement.
25 of 34 items without a vendor mention makes share-of-voice unreliable.
One Gcore example does not establish broad regional adoption.
Sentiment percentages describe this sample, not the customer population.

test_case.title: Customer sentiment, adoption signals, and evidence quality across Europe and the US

expected_findings.finding: The analysis covers cloud service providers and AI developers, NVIDIA, Broadcom, Intel, Europe, and the United States.
expected_findings.primary_claim: The analysis covers cloud service providers and AI developers, NVIDIA, Broadcom, Intel, Europe, and the United States.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis covers cloud service providers and AI developers, NVIDIA, Broadcom, Intel, Europe, and the United States.

expected_findings.finding: The 34-item sample contains 24 positive (70.6%), 7 neutral (20.6%), 2 negative (5.9%), and 1 mixed (2.9%) items; this is not population-wide sentiment.
expected_findings.primary_claim: The 34-item sample contains 24 positive (70.6%), 7 neutral (20.6%), 2 negative (5.9%), and 1 mixed (2.9%) items; this is not population-wide sentiment.
acceptance_criteria: The 34-item sample contains 24 positive (70.6%), 7 neutral (20.6%), 2 negative (5.9%), and 1 mixed (2.9%) items; this is not population-wide sentiment.

expected_findings.finding: Broadcom's Google and Meta AI-chip collaborations are a low-confidence positive signal based only on news snippets.
expected_findings.primary_claim: Broadcom's Google and Meta AI-chip collaborations are a low-confidence positive signal based only on news snippets.
acceptance_criteria: Broadcom's Google and Meta AI-chip collaborations are a low-confidence positive signal based only on news snippets.
